text: 据外媒报道，马来西亚正考虑允许部分未加工稀土出口，以巩固其在从汽车制造到国防和消费品等行业的供应链地位。马来西亚在2024年暂停了未加工稀土出口，以刺激对国内加工业的投资——这是资源丰富的发展中国家常见的策略。但据一位高级政府官员称，随着围绕这些矿产的竞争加剧，当局目前正在评估放松限制的可行性。马来西亚自然资源与环境可持续发展部副部长Syed表示：“任何新的出口都将附带条件，包括与入境投资和技术转让挂钩。”他拒绝给出出口法规调整的时间表。赛义德称，马来西亚拥有1610万吨的“推断储量”稀土。政府此前曾表示，这些储量可能价值9700亿林吉特（2370亿美元
text_en: According to foreign media, Malaysia is considering allowing some unprocessed rare earth exports to consolidate its supply chain position from auto manufacturing to defense and consumer goods. Malaysia suspended unprocessed rare earth exports in 2024 to spur domestic processing investment—a common strategy for resource-rich developing countries. But per a senior government official, as competition over these minerals intensifies, authorities are assessing the feasibility of easing restrictions. Malaysia's Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Syed said: "Any new exports will come with conditions, including links to inbound investment and technology transfer." He declined to give a timeline for export regulation changes. Syed said Malaysia has 16.1 million tons of "inferred reserves" of rare earths.
